The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria says it has uncovered 250 fake teaching certificates during a recruitment exercise, prompting the rollout of Quick Response (QR)-coded certificates and stricter digital verification. The Chief Executive and Registrar of TRCN, Dr Ronke Soyombo, said the move was aimed at flushing out quacks from Nigerian classrooms. Soyombo disclosed this while monitoring the ongoing computer-based Professional Qualifying Examination (PQE) at Redeemer’s TEAP International School, Abuja, on Thursday. She revealed that the council made the discovery during a recruitment process in which an unidentified state sought to employ about 1,000 teachers. She warned that forged credentials posed a grave threat to the nation’s education standards. To curb the circulation of fake certificates, she explained that TRCN now issues certificates embedded with QR codes that link employers directly to the council’s portal for instant authentication before recruitment. Beyond weeding out unqualified personnel, Soyombo noted that the Federal Government had set a strict deadline to ensure that 75 per cent of teachers were licensed by the end of 2026 and 100 per cent were certified before entering any classroom by December 2027. Commending the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, for backing the mandatory certification drive, the registrar stressed that a first-class degree alone did not qualify an individual to teach without proven competence in pedagogy, child safeguarding and digital literacy. Soyombo also disclosed that previous PQE assessments exposed widespread weaknesses in mathematics among teachers nationwide, prompting the council to design targeted training interventions with relevant education agencies. Soyombo urged candidates to shun malpractice and fraudulent shortcuts, reiterating that TRCN would sustain its digital clampdown to protect Nigerian schoolchildren and raise teaching standards. Some of the candidates who spoke with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) described the computer-based exercise as well-coordinated. One of them, Ms Celestina Adejo, said the questions had sharpened her knowledge of child safeguarding and ICT security. A Nigerian Navy education officer, Ebi Mustapha, and a teacher with 27 years of classroom experience, Esther Ali, said they sat for the examination to validate their professional competence, urging other practitioners to get certified. Another candidate, Benjamin Edet, however, recommended that examination slips should directly display assigned centres and schedules to eliminate delays associated with WhatsApp groups and external links. Meanwhile, the CBT Coordinator and ICT Administrator at the school, Mrs Ann Ogbu, said the centre had deployed a 60kVA solar system, a 250kVA backup generator and 20 standby computers out of its 220 systems to guarantee hitch-free testing. Ogbu said the Garki-based facility, which was expanding to 320 computers, had conducted successful demonstration tests with TRCN’s technical team to ensure seamless server connectivity throughout the exercise. She added that hosting major examinations for TRCN, the West African Examinations Council, the National Examinations Council and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs showcased the school’s modern ICT infrastructure and commitment to quality education.
